text: At the quarterly retro I told everyone that the decision to postpone the Postgres migration had been mine and that it cost us two weeks of rework. I'd rather own the mistake in front of everyone than let the team think the problem was their planning. After that, our conversations about estimates became much more candid.

tags.quote: own the mistake in front of everyone

text: I spent a good part of Tuesday reviewing next semester's cloud budget with the finance team. I also took the chance to update the cost-per-service spreadsheet and schedule the renewal of our observability tool licenses.

The release 4.2 planning was turning into a shouting match over estimates when Sofia stopped everything, listed the three decisions that had to come out of that meeting and gave each person two minutes to speak. We left in forty minutes with scope closed and owners assigned for every epic. It's impressive how meetings with her in charge end with decisions made.

tags.quote: listed the three decisions that had to come out of that meeting and gave each person two minutes to speak

text: I agreed with Sofia that the billing service tech debt would go into the next sprint and, I admit, I let it slip. On Monday she showed up at my desk with the agreement written down and asked me what I needed to hit the deadline. With her, nothing we agree on in a meeting ever falls through the cracks.

tags.quote: nothing we agree on in a meeting ever falls through the cracks

text: In the post-mortem for the gateway outage, Sofia opened by saying she herself had approved the deploy without a contingency window, before anyone could point fingers. That changed the tone of the room instantly: everyone started describing what they did without fear. The final document came out with five action items and no scapegoats.

tags.quote: she herself had approved the deploy without a contingency window
everyone started describing what they did without fear

text: When the commitment to cover the regression tests before the freeze started slipping, Sofia pulled me and Tomás in and rebuilt the plan with dates and owners in front of everyone. The following week she came back to the topic in the daily herself to check on progress, item by item.

tags.quote: rebuilt the plan with dates and owners in front of everyone

text: In my first sprint I was lost between three demands, and Sofia set up a quick session with Caio and Marina to align priorities and split up who would support me on what. In half an hour everyone left knowing exactly their part. She has a way of organizing people that just makes the work move.

tags.quote: set up a quick session with Caio and Marina to align priorities and split up who would support me on what

text: Bruno and Tomás had been stuck for two days arguing whether the notifications service should use a queue or webhooks, and the mood in the channel had already soured. I pulled the two of them into a room, asked each one to write the trade-offs on the whiteboard and proposed a one-day load test to decide with numbers. They left to have lunch together and the decision came the next day.

tags.quote: I pulled the two of them into a room, asked each one to write the trade-offs on the whiteboard

text: In the discussion about carving up the monolith, André and I were already trading jabs in a thread when Marina stepped in, summarized both sides with impressive neutrality and suggested taking the matter to the RFC instead of the chat. The tension died right there and the RFC got approved with no hard feelings.

tags.quote: summarized both sides with impressive neutrality

text: I handed Marina the log audit epic with a tight deadline because of the certification. She broke it into weekly deliverables, flagged on Wednesday that one item would slip two days and made it up on the next one. She closed the epic on the agreed date, with no surprises at all.

tags.quote: She closed the epic on the agreed date, with no surprises at all.

text: There was a week when product and engineering got stuck over the export report deadline, with people complaining on both sides. Marina offered to sit down with me and João and translated the fight into two scope options with realistic dates. A meeting that promised to be tense ended in agreement in twenty minutes.

tags.quote: translated the fight into two scope options with realistic dates

text: I shared the new office workbench with Marina during the third-floor renovation. We ended up syncing our focus hours and the rotation for the small meeting room. Other than that, it was an ordinary sprint week.

When Letícia got buried in design system bugs right before the freeze, Marina noticed before I did and took on two fixes without anyone asking. She has also been my thermometer for the team: when a technical discussion starts heating up, she steps in and brings everyone back to the problem. She is the person who keeps the temperature of the room in check.

tags.quote: took on two fixes without anyone asking
when a technical discussion starts heating up, she steps in and brings everyone back to the problem

text: Before we approved switching the event bus, I built a matrix comparing cost, latency and maturity across the three options and ran a weekend prototype with real data. The result knocked out the option that was my favorite, and it was the first one I discarded. I'd rather lose a personal bet than push a decision without evidence.

tags.quote: built a matrix comparing cost, latency and maturity across the three options
I'd rather lose a personal bet than push a decision without evidence

text: This sprint I was on interview duty for the technical loops and reviewed the system design question script with the recruiting folks. I also migrated my architecture notes to the new wiki. Busy week, but nothing out of the ordinary.

My first code review at Lumina came back with seventeen comments from Caio and none of them was just 'change this': each one explained the why and linked an example in our codebase. Afterwards he set aside half an hour to pair with me on the concurrency part I hadn't understood. In two months I grew more than in the entire previous year.

tags.quote: each one explained the why and linked an example in our codebase

text: In the design of the new permissions API, Caio was the only one who asked what would happen when the cache expired mid-session, and he dismantled the proposal with two scenarios nobody had considered. We redid the design and avoided what would have been a guaranteed incident in production.

tags.quote: dismantled the proposal with two scenarios nobody had considered

text: When I took over the event pipeline, Caio put together a three-week study plan with me and reviewed my diagrams every Friday, always pointing out where my reasoning skipped a step. He doesn't give you the answer: he asks the question that forces you to find it yourself.

tags.quote: put together a three-week study plan with me and reviewed my diagrams every Friday

text: As a PM, I've seen tech leads let roadmap agreements evaporate, but with Caio it's the opposite: he records every commitment from the sprint review and follows up, including with me, when something drifts. Last quarter he called me in to publicly renegotiate an item engineering wasn't going to deliver, instead of letting it die quietly.

tags.quote: he records every commitment from the sprint review and follows up, including with me, when something drifts

text: Caio instituted a biweekly review of technical debt items on the team and won't let an item leave the list without an owner and a date. When the messaging queue discussion heated up, he brought benchmarks and a failure comparison before giving an opinion. He is my most reliable counterpoint on hard decisions.

tags.quote: won't let an item leave the list without an owner and a date
brought benchmarks and a failure comparison before giving an opinion

text: I picked up the billing service rewrite in January with a commitment to flip the switch before the fiscal close. I sliced the migration into seven deliverables, posted progress every Friday in the channel and we cut over with three days to spare. There was no heroism, just the plan being executed week after week.

tags.quote: I sliced the migration into seven deliverables, posted progress every Friday in the channel and we cut over with three days to spare

text: Reviewing one of Bruno's PRs, I noticed he had left comments in his own code flagging two timezone edge cases that not even my tests covered. He also attached to the description a table with the cent-rounding scenarios he had validated manually. It's rare for QA to find anything after he reviews his own work.

tags.quote: flagging two timezone edge cases that not even my tests covered

text: I split the new payment provider integration with Bruno and we agreed he would deliver the reconciliation layer by the 20th. On the 18th it was in production behind a feature flag, with a runbook written. Working with him means being able to plan on his word.

tags.quote: On the 18th it was in production behind a feature flag, with a runbook written

text: Every month-end I depend on the reconciliation job Bruno maintains to close the operations numbers. On one of those closes he alerted me to a four-cent discrepancy the old system had been ignoring for months, along with the query proving its origin. We closed the month without a manual adjustment for the first time this year.

tags.quote: alerted me to a four-cent discrepancy the old system had been ignoring for months

text: For the office move, Bruno took charge of labeling the workbench equipment and organizing the spare cables in the cabinet. We also took the opportunity to update the monitor inventory with the facilities folks.

Over the last six sprints Bruno delivered everything he pulled, and when he realized the idempotency story was bigger than it looked, he flagged it in Monday's daily and replanned with me, not at the last minute. It's the kind of predictability that lets me sleep soundly during release week.

tags.quote: Over the last six sprints Bruno delivered everything he pulled

text: Before releasing the new invoices screen, I put together a checklist of the empty, error and loading states across three screen sizes, and found a layout overflow that only showed up with very long company names. I fixed it and added the case to the visual test suite so it wouldn't come back.

tags.quote: found a layout overflow that only showed up with very long company names

text: I was drowning trying to finish the onboarding form and hadn't even asked for help when Letícia showed up with a draft branch solving the validation part that was blocking me. She had noticed from the channel that I was going in circles. She then stayed with me until the end of the day reviewing the rest.

tags.quote: hadn't even asked for help when Letícia showed up with a draft branch

text: In the export flow review, Letícia listed eight inconsistencies in date and currency masks across screens that had been slipping through for months. Everything came documented with screenshots and step-by-step reproduction. My QA work yields twice as much when the PR is hers.

tags.quote: listed eight inconsistencies in date and currency masks across screens

text: I delivered the redesign of the table components and Letícia returned an implementation with spacing and focus states faithful to the spec down to the pixel, including a keyboard state I myself had forgotten to design. She even pointed out two inconsistencies in my Figma file.

tags.quote: including a keyboard state I myself had forgotten to design

text: I heard Letícia took over organizing the team's World Cup pool and the schedule for the Friday demo rotation. In this week's dailies we only synced on merging the release branch, a quiet week.

Twice this quarter Letícia reshuffled her own tasks to rescue swamped teammates, once on the checkout accessibility fixes and once on the freeze bug queue, without me having to ask. And she remains the person who catches the most visual problems before QA even takes a look.

tags.quote: reshuffled her own tasks to rescue swamped teammates
the person who catches the most visual problems before QA even takes a look

text: When the production cluster started killing pods at 3 a.m., I opened the incident call, assigned who would look at the database and who would look at the network, and narrated every hypothesis we tested in the channel. In forty minutes we isolated the memory leak, and only then did I go figure out why the alert was late. Panic doesn't diagnose anything.

tags.quote: I opened the incident call, assigned who would look at the database and who would look at the network, and narrated every hypothesis we tested in the channel

text: I finished documenting the access key rotation process and updated the network topology diagram on the wiki. I also left the quarterly maintenance of the CI runners scheduled for the holiday.

On the Friday of the DNS provider blackout, with half the platform down and sales panicking in the general channel, André kept replying in the same tone as always, listing what we already knew and what still needed confirming. He asked for ten minutes of operational silence, applied the failover and we were back before the SLA blew.

tags.quote: kept replying in the same tone as always, listing what we already knew and what still needed confirming

text: The flaky test that kept breaking our deploy wasn't even André's domain, but it bothered him, so he traced the cause down to a race condition in the sessions service and opened the fix along with a new alert. He carried the problem all the way to the end when he could have just forwarded the ticket.

tags.quote: traced the cause down to a race condition in the sessions service and opened the fix along with a new alert

text: I work on the support front line and have been in several war rooms with André. In the December queue overflow, he gave me updates every fifteen minutes with what I could relay internally, without a note of stress in his voice. The recovery estimate he gave was off by only ten minutes.

tags.quote: without a note of stress in his voice
The recovery estimate he gave was off by only ten minutes

text: André promised the observability migration wouldn't cause a single minute of downtime and delivered exactly that, with a rollback plan rehearsed in staging twice. The new dashboards became a reference for the whole team.

tags.quote: delivered exactly that, with a rollback plan rehearsed in staging twice

text: In the replica database incident, André took command without me having to assign anyone, coordinated three people with a calm that soothed even folks outside engineering, and then wrote the most thorough post-mortem I have ever received. He treats any platform problem as his own until someone formally takes it over.

tags.quote: He treats any platform problem as his own
a calm that soothed even folks outside engineering

text: We needed to swap the pipeline orchestrator and I had never touched Airflow. I spent a weekend with the documentation and a toy cluster, and on Wednesday I presented a comparison based on what I had actually tested, including the points where my initial hypothesis was wrong. I changed my recommendation halfway through the study because the numbers didn't support the first one.

tags.quote: I changed my recommendation halfway through the study because the numbers didn't support the first one
I presented a comparison based on what I had actually tested

text: On the proposal to double the data cluster, Paula asked for a week, came back with a cost-per-query analysis and showed the bottleneck was a badly partitioned join, not capacity. We saved the entire expansion because she wouldn't accept the obvious diagnosis.

tags.quote: showed the bottleneck was a badly partitioned join, not capacity

text: Paula and I shared the presentation slot at last month's all-hands to show the internal roadmap for the data platform. We rehearsed the day before in the big room and everything went fine with the new projector.

I asked Paula for help with a data cross-reference for my latest study and discovered she had taught herself, in two weeks, the statistical analysis library my team took months to adopt. She even sent me back a reproducible notebook commenting on every decision in the model.

tags.quote: taught herself, in two weeks, the statistical analysis library

text: When we migrated the events to the new schema, Paula was the only one who had never worked with Protobuf, and within ten days she was already reviewing my PRs, pointing out compatibility gotchas I didn't know about. She turns documentation into practice at an impressive speed.

tags.quote: within ten days she was already reviewing my PRs

text: Before any expensive decision on the data platform I run it by Paula: she breaks the proposal down into assumptions, tests the ones that can be tested and hands me back the risk in numbers. That's how we avoided signing an oversized warehouse contract last quarter.

tags.quote: she breaks the proposal down into assumptions, tests the ones that can be tested and hands me back the risk in numbers

text: I joined Lumina having never touched Go, and three months later I was running the reprocessing worker on my own. I kept an error journal of my first weeks and went back to it every Friday so I wouldn't repeat the same stumbles. What helped me most was asking for review early, before the code was pretty.

tags.quote: I joined Lumina having never touched Go, and three months later I was running the reprocessing worker on my own

text: The task force to cut build time had been dragging on for two sprints until Diego rallied a one-afternoon blitz, with a scoreboard of minutes saved on the whiteboard. His energy won over even the people who had said they had no time, and the build dropped from 22 to 9 minutes that week.

tags.quote: rallied a one-afternoon blitz, with a scoreboard of minutes saved on the whiteboard

text: I borrowed Diego to help me on the front end for a sprint and he had never touched React. By the third day he was already opening decent PRs, and by the end of the sprint he fixed a state bug on his own that would have taken me an afternoon. He writes everything down and never asks the same question twice.

tags.quote: By the third day he was already opening decent PRs

text: I needed an API prototype to validate the reports flow before the roadmap review and Diego volunteered on the spot, put the skeleton together the same day and kept sending me updates in the evening without me asking. His pace unblocked a discussion that had been stalled for two weeks.

tags.quote: put the skeleton together the same day and kept sending me updates in the evening without me asking

text: Diego took charge of updating the on-call rotation in the shared calendar after the team's timezone change. Together we double-checked the semester's holidays and adjusted the agreed swaps.

Diego is the junior who got off training wheels fastest on the team: in four months he went from guided tasks to driving the modernization of the queue jobs on his own. In plannings he is always the first to volunteer, and more than once his enthusiasm pulled the sprint out of inertia after a rough week.

tags.quote: in four months he went from guided tasks to driving the modernization of the queue jobs on his own
more than once his enthusiasm pulled the sprint out of inertia

text: During the 4.1 release regression, I got suspicious about a one-pixel difference in the totals column and pulled the thread: it was a rounding issue that added up wrong only on invoices with installment discounts. I wrote the test case, mapped the three affected screens and held the release until the fix landed.

tags.quote: got suspicious about a one-pixel difference in the totals column and pulled the thread
held the release until the fix landed

text: I spent the morning reorganizing the test evidence repository by release and archiving the old plans. In the afternoon I attended the semester's mandatory information security training.

I thought my billing module PR was bulletproof until Renata sent back a script with fourteen scenarios, including a leap-year month rollover that broke the pro rata calculation. She even had test data ready to reproduce it. Nothing gets past her.

tags.quote: a leap-year month rollover that broke the pro rata calculation

text: At the start of the freeze we agreed no critical bug would go to production without a full regression, and when I tried to open an exception 'just this once', Renata reminded me of the agreement in front of the team and proposed a path that fit the deadline. She holds everyone to what was agreed, senior folks included.

tags.quote: reminded me of the agreement in front of the team and proposed a path that fit the deadline

text: I forwarded engineering some odd behavior in the consumption report and Renata was the one who took the case. She reproduced the scenario with three configuration combinations I didn't even know existed and sent me back a step-by-step of what was wrong in each one. The ticket came back more complete than I sent it.

tags.quote: reproduced the scenario with three configuration combinations I didn't even know existed

text: Renata owns our definition of done: when the team started loosening the minimum coverage on end-of-quarter deliveries, she brought the numbers to the retro and got us to renew the agreement in writing. Since then she is the one who audits, release by release, whether we are keeping what we signed.

tags.quote: brought the numbers to the retro and got us to renew the agreement in writing

text: I took on delivering the export module with a date promised for the quarter close, and I cut two improvements I had proposed myself when I saw they put the date at risk. We delivered on the agreed day and the improvements went into the following sprint. I'd rather ship the essentials on time than everything late.

tags.quote: We delivered on the agreed day
I cut two improvements I had proposed myself when I saw they put the date at risk

text: I upgraded my machine to the new container-based development setup and took the chance to re-record the technical onboarding video that had been outdated since last year. I also replaced the keyboard that was failing.

Every quarter we bet on who delivers what they planned, and with Tomás it's not even fun: over the last four releases he nailed the scope without slipping a single day. When the PDF service threatened to run late, he renegotiated the cut on Monday, not the day before the demo.

tags.quote: over the last four releases he nailed the scope without slipping a single day

text: In the dispute over which squad would own the reports service, Tomás gave up a project that would clearly have earned him the spotlight because the other path unblocked the release for the whole team. He presented the transition plan himself. Ego doesn't enter the equation for him when the team's goal is at stake.

tags.quote: gave up a project that would clearly have earned him the spotlight because the other path unblocked the release for the whole team

text: Whenever Tomás hands me a deploy window, I block my calendar without a second thought: the artifact arrives tested, with the rollback checklist filled out and at the time he said. In two years of on-call together, I have never had to chase him.

tags.quote: the artifact arrives tested, with the rollback checklist filled out and at the time he said

text: The revenue recognition report depended on an extraction engineering never prioritized, until Tomás took it on. He delivered the first version to me on the Friday he promised and automated the monthly send without me asking. I close the financials two days earlier because of it.

tags.quote: He delivered the first version to me on the Friday he promised

text: When I had to choose who would carry the certification release delivery, I chose Tomás and he reprioritized the squad's backlog around the date, pulling even his own items out of the way. He is the person I use as my benchmark for predictability when I negotiate deadlines with other areas.

tags.quote: reprioritized the squad's backlog around the date, pulling even his own items out of the way
benchmark for predictability when I negotiate deadlines with other areas
